newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds rally, becoming wary over rates.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds rally, becoming wary over rates.

text.p: *Australian bonds rallied amid a technical short squeeze, although the outlook for official interest rates is becoming somewhat clouded by the sustained weakness in the local dollar.
*U.S. faces barrage of data later on Wednesday.
Australian bonds rallied amid a technical short squeeze, although the outlook for official interest rates is becoming somewhat clouded by the sustained weakness in the local dollar.

The market's bounce coincided with a modest recovery in the Australian currency after being quoted at a fresh 18-month intra-day low of US$0.7310/15 at one stage, although the risk of an easing in monetary easing continues to hang on the unit.
"Although, if the Aussie remains at these levels, I think you can put (a rate cut) on the back-burner for now," said Chris Bell, Treasury Director at Dresdner Australia.

The reaction to the plight of the currency was more evident at the short end of the debt curve where September bill futures briefly slipped to 94.77 and over 20 basis points below the contract peak of 94.99 seen after last week's labour force data.
But even at the low the market still had a 1/4 point easing priced in in current 5.5 percent official rates.

Meanwhile, the government continued to try and dampen down rate cut hopes with Prime Minister John Howard saying he had not been calling for an easing in monetary policy when he said last week that he wanted to see lower interest rates.
Although the market briefly dipped on Howard's rate retraction, the move lacked follow through with the market finding itself short after the initial currency-led sell-off.
Thoughts of an easing helped the Westpac-Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index rise 1.1 points in July, partly correcting the 5.8 percent drop in the preceding three months.

"The recovery...rests heavily on a rise in confidence about the current state of household finances, reflecting a lagged response to the latest interest rate cut and reaction to the growing speculation of yet another cut to come in the near future," said Westpac chief economist Nigel Stapledon.
"The Reserve Bank is expected to validate that speculation with a rate cut sometime in the next few weeks," he added.

Although currency weakness may have muddied the interest rate outlook over the past few days, traders said the market remains confident that next week's data will confirm the forecast benign outcome for second quarter inflation, along with an expected acceptable level of wages growth.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury market faces a barrage of data later on Wednesday with the release of June CPI, along with business inventories, industrial production, and capacity utilisation for May.

The technical rebound saw yield spreads reverse an early widening to the U.S. and saw the market testing support at 40 basis points. A breach here could open the way to a further contraction to a major level of 25 b.p. N.Z. yields rose sharply to firm up monetary conditions as the N.Z. dollar fell.
